solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rubbish lad can cite by chance

indicators.note: as a verb, to rubbish something is to trash it, so the letters that follow are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a boy who can quote things only by luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens by chance is unplanned, which is what an accidental event is; the adjective and the adverbial phrase both describe luck.

clue.text: Provide family pet with little hesitation

parts.note: the short sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: Supplying a household animal, with only a brief pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food or whatever else is needed, a close synonym of provide.

clue.text: Popular old stage turn is not quite on the mark

parts.note: a turn on stage is an act

explanation.surface: A well-loved old variety act no longer quite hits the target.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise, slightly off, so it describes something not quite on target.

clue.text: Appearing regularly, hen like a large deer

indicators.note: something appearing at regular intervals shows up every other time, so only alternate letters are kept

explanation.surface: A chicken is oddly said to resemble a big deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk is one of the largest species of the deer family, also called moose in Europe.

clue.text: Maybe turn to French trains: one's missing, delayed!

indicators.note: one is the Roman numeral I, and missing says it is absent from the word before

explanation.surface: A complaint about French railways: a train has vanished and the rest are running behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that turning a text into French is only one example of the answer, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering a text into French is an example of converting words from one language to another.

clue.text: Some in Geneva elected to return for holiday

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters are read backwards
only some of the letters inside the following words are wanted

parts.note: found across the end of Geneva and the start of elected

explanation.surface: Some Swiss politicians were voted back in time for their holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off work, as in annual leave, which is a holiday.

clue.text: Eleven of Glasgow's clubs, etc I left drunk

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers around, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tale of a night out in Glasgow's nightclubs, leaving drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests nightlife but is the card suit. Celtic is one of Glasgow's two big football clubs, and a football team has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic Football Club is a Glasgow team, and a football side fields eleven players.

clue.text: Flash diner finally tucking into some beef?

indicators.note: tucking into food means going inside it, so one piece is placed within another
finally points to the last letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A smart restaurant guest finally starts eating a piece of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like an adjective for the diner but is the verb: to flash or streak is to run past naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, and flashing is likewise exposing oneself.

clue.text: Centrepiece of magazine: a field and a flower

indicators.note: the centrepiece is what sits in the middle, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the middle two of its eight letters
lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: A magazine's central feature shows a meadow and a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: LEA, a meadow, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The azalea is a flowering shrub related to rhododendrons, prized for its bright blooms.

clue.text: Live west of a neighbourhood

indicators.note: in an across answer, west means to the left, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to be or exist; 'they are' means they live

explanation.surface: Advice on residing on the western side of some district.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district, such as the part of town where someone lives.

clue.text: Ready to enter class bringing tape

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A pupil prepared to come into the classroom carrying a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a small case of magnetic tape for recording sound or video.

clue.text: Arthropod that could make decent pie!

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim joke about a many-legged creature as a good pie filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A centipede is a many-legged invertebrate with a jointed body, which places it among the arthropods.

clue.text: Fabric from bed not put back

parts.note: a small bed, often for a baby

indicators.note: putting something back returns it the way it came, so the word is written backwards

explanation.surface: Material taken from a bed that nobody returned to its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is cloth woven from the fibres of the cotton plant, a common fabric.

clue.text: Alternatively, register brought up for the Speaker

indicators.note: in a down answer, bringing something up lifts it bottom to top, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list or roster of names

explanation.surface: Instead, a record is raised for the Speaker of the House to consider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' suggests the presiding officer of Parliament; here it is just anyone who gives speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is someone who delivers public speeches, that is, a speaker.

clue.text: Junkie put on island by court

parts.note: to put on is to add

explanation.surface: A drug user is sent to an island by a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A junkie is slang for a drug addict, someone dependent on a substance.

clue.text: Skilful, grasping old company's shortfall

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British industrial giant

explanation.surface: A greedy, clever firm of yesteryear has a hole in its accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British chemicals firm taken over in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is the amount by which money or supply falls short of what is needed.

clue.text: Support team that's bottom

parts.note: a sports team is a side

explanation.surface: Cheering on the club that is last in the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' reads as last in the table, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside is an informal word for the buttocks, also called the bottom.

clue.text: What's needed to open vehicle, some say, a shade military

indicators.note: what some people say is heard rather than read, so the answer matches a sound

parts.note: you need one to unlock a car

explanation.surface: Talk of a car key and a somewhat soldierly look.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the r of car is silent, so the two words match the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is the dull brownish-green colour used for army uniforms.

clue.text: Lover consuming large tart

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a lover of something is a fan

explanation.surface: An enthusiast eating a big pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling, which is a type of tart.

clue.text: Keen expert outside but losing head

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other
losing its head means the word drops its first letter

explanation.surface: An eager specialist is still beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' looks like a mere conjunction in the surface, yet it is the word that gets beheaded and wrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute senses are sharp, and keen eyesight or hearing is acute.

clue.text: Party time following second supply of drug

indicators.note: following means coming after, so one piece is placed behind the other

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Party-goers get a second round of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured amount of a medicine given, so it is the supply of a drug.

clue.text: Minor problem with husband in charge of trophy

explanation.surface: A small hitch when the husband is put in charge of the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is figuratively a small temporary setback or minor problem.

clue.text: Greeting, over time, success

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means above, so the first piece sits on top of the next

explanation.surface: A hello, given over time, eventually pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit is a successful song, show or venture, so it means a success.

clue.text: Lots of distinctive characteristics: one impression one matches

parts.note: a dent is an impression in a surface
drawn games, or things that match

explanation.surface: Personality traits listed like an impressionist's set of matching voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Identities are the sets of distinguishing features that make individuals who they are.
